about: Words the matcher uses, as data. Phrases are matched as whole words, without regard to case. Each list names where its words come from: the project owner's matching rules and cases (docs: rule N / case N) or the design (DESIGN 3.3). The app does not grade condition (owner decision 2026-10-19); eBay's own condition text is shown as it is.

specUnits.source: owner rule 24 and case 7 (DC-600 KHZ, 0-1500V, 50kv, 10Hz-50 MHz, 100:1, 15 MEG, 4 channels); GHz, mA, mV, VAC, VDC added in the phase-4 review (frequency ranges of signal generators and mains voltages are written that way)

notModels.source: phase-4 review: model-like words that are counts, decades, ordinals or versions, not model codes

notBrands.source: phase-4 review: Brand values that name no brand; the user is asked instead

lot.source: owner rule 4 ("lot of", quantities), case 1 (LOT OF 13 ...); DESIGN 3.3 (2x)

partWords.source: owner rule 14 (several model codes + part words: knobs, feet, cover, cord) and case 4; alone they do not make a part (a title saying the item needs a cord is the item)

kitWords.source: owner case 9 ("RECAP KIT"; "kit"/"set" with component types): the word that makes a kit; alone it decides nothing, because the brand's own kits of complete devices are the item

kitParts.source: owner case 9: repair/upgrade kits and parts sets for the model (recap, cap, capacitor, rebuild, restoration, repair, upgrade, parts kit; component types capacitors, diodes, resistors, transistors, tubes, knobs); with a kit word -> part/fits

kitFor.source: owner case 9: "kit for" is a kit for something, not the item

completeKit.source: owner case 9 ("Heathkit IP-20 kit unbuilt": an unbuilt complete brand kit IS the item); a kit with none of these and no parts word is "to check"

withItem.source: owner case 1: the real comp "... w/ Leads" is the item with its leads; "in" ("in original case") added in the phase-4 review; "and" is not one ("Operation and Calibration Manual" is documentation)

likelyBroken.source: owner decision 2026-10-19 "red flag likely broken" (verbatim list): words meaning it was not tested or works only partly - all mean broken; a warning only, never grading

partsConditions.source: owner decision 2026-10-19 "red flag likely broken": eBay's own condition wording
